clue.text: The boxer is running round the ring. What's up?

indicators.note: running round suggests moving about in circles, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: a ring is round, so it gives the letter O
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A fighter circles the ring while someone asks what the matter is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running round' rearranges O (the ring) together with WHATSUP. A southpaw is a boxer who leads with the right hand and punches with the left.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is a left-handed fighter, so it names a particular kind of boxer.

clue.text: Lays hands on some blunt weapons

definitions.meaning: provides workers (hands) for, as an employer mans a firm
cudgels or poles used to strike with

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' here means workers, not fingers and palms.
explanation.definitionFit: To man a business with workers is one sense; clubs or cudgels carried as weapons is the other.

clue.text: Knock off at sunset and have a meal

indicators.note: set read as arranged or put in place, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: to have a meal is to eat

explanation.surface: A worker stops for the day as evening falls and goes off to dine.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'sunset' as one word but the wordplay reads it as 'sun set': 'set' rearranges SUN to UNS, then EAT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock a rider off a horse is to throw them from the saddle.

clue.text: Wait for the idol of yesteryear to come in

indicators.note: to come in means one piece enters the middle of the other

parts.note: a hit is a popular success, a favourite of the public
something of yesteryear is old

explanation.surface: A fan waits for a faded star of the past to make an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come in' puts OLD inside HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase is a command telling someone to stop and hold on.

clue.text: Quite a number got upset by the anaesthetic

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word got upside down, so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written
ether was an early general anaesthetic

explanation.surface: Many patients were made queasy by the gas used in surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GOT into TOG. 'Number' is the Roman fifty, L, not a count.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean completely or entirely, as in 'not quite finished'.

clue.text: In a fury, I put back the queen

indicators.note: put back means the whole assembly is turned to read the other way
In says the letter I sits within the word for fury

parts.note: a fury is a fit of anger

explanation.surface: Someone in a rage puts the queen back down, as in a game of chess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts I inside ANGER to give ANGIER, and 'put back' turns that round. Regina is Latin for queen, as in the 'R' of a monarch's signature.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is the Latin title used for a reigning female monarch.

clue.text: Out of money, barter

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-directory
change is coins or small money

explanation.surface: Having run out of cash, someone trades goods instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Bartering is swapping goods without money, a form of trade.

clue.text: Found one tin damaged and I polished it off

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: damaged means the word tin is knocked out of shape and rearranged

parts.note: to polish off food is to eat it all

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a dented can and finishes what was in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' turns TIN into NIT. 'Found' is the verb meaning set up, not the past of find.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to start or establish it.

clue.text: For a bet, run with one of the world's fastest runners

definitions.text: one of the world's fastest runners

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up before cards are dealt
to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes money on a race between sprinters.
explanation.definitionFit: This African horned grazer is famous for its great speed across the plains.

clue.text: Bales out-a complete disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in a wreck, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A pilot ejecting from a plane is a total catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges BALESOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means total or utter, as in absolute nonsense.

clue.text: Paper with lines on it

parts.note: reads like ruled writing paper, but means the pages an actor's spoken part is written on

explanation.walkthrough: The lines are those an actor speaks, not ruled lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A play's text is the paper carrying the performers' speeches.

clue.text: A bird hopping round

parts.note: hopping mad means furious, as does flaming
round is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A bird bounces about in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopping' looks like the bird's movement, but stands for 'hopping mad', furious.
explanation.definitionFit: This pink wading bird is a long-legged waterfowl.

clue.text: Making a comeback in the starring role about a biblical character

indicators.note: making a comeback means the whole arrangement returns, read backwards
about means the role goes around the little word in

parts.note: the lead is the main part in a play

explanation.surface: An actor returns in a leading part, playing someone from scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IN inside LEAD to give LEINAD, which 'Making a comeback' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The prophet thrown into the lions' den is an Old Testament figure.

clue.text: Miss home mostly at weekends?

parts.note: a young woman who is home only at weekends because her job takes up the week

explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb (to miss home) but is a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman devoted to her profession is mostly at work, home only at weekends.

clue.text: A vertical take-off. Honestly

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means directly upwards, and is also slang for 'really, truly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket rising vertically goes this way; an earnest assurance uses the same phrase.

clue.text: Makes as though to go, but doesn't keep the appointment

definitions.meaning: rises from a seat as if to leave
fails to turn up for a date

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is getting to your feet; the other is failing to show up for a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising to your feet to leave and leaving a date waiting are both covered by the phrase.

clue.text: Compromise, to restore good relations

parts.note: restoring good relations means putting a stop to bad feeling, a finish to rage
restoring good relations means putting a stop to bad feeling, a finish to rage

explanation.surface: Both sides give ground so that friendship can be mended.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read as 'end anger'. 'Compromise' is the verb meaning put at risk, not a settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise someone's safety is to put it at risk.

clue.text: Is not indelible, it is revealed

definitions.meaning: washes away, as a stain does

explanation.walkthrough: A stain that washes off and a secret that becomes known are both described by the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A washable mark lifts off in laundering, and news that emerges becomes public.

clue.text: Accommodation, even so, will be arranged in time

parts.note: a tent is shelter for campers

indicators.note: will be arranged signals that the letters of even so are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Lodging will still be sorted out in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be arranged' rearranges EVENSO into OSEVEN after TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock reading just before seven is a particular moment of the day.

clue.text: Back on board

parts.note: reads as returning to a ship, but means towards the rear of a vessel

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests returning to a ship; it is the sailor's word for behind.
explanation.definitionFit: At or towards the stern is the rear direction on a ship.

clue.text: One can't run out of it

definitions.text: One can't run out of it

parts.words: One can't run out of it
parts.note: a person who is gasping and puffed cannot keep running

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a supply that never ends, but means you cannot run when you are puffed.
explanation.definitionFit: Air drawn into the lungs is what runners need to keep going.

clue.text: A break in the depression

definitions.meaning: a pause, as when parliament or school stops
a hollow or niche in a wall

explanation.walkthrough: A break from work and an alcove set back in a wall share the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday interval and a hollow alcove are both meanings.

clue.text: Easier to touch, though harder to borrow from

definitions.meaning: more stingy, from a dialect sense of near meaning mean with money

explanation.walkthrough: Near also means mean or tight-fisted, so a nearer person is harder to borrow from.
explanation.definitionFit: Closer in distance is one sense; tighter with money is the other.

clue.text: Keep quiet when brought to book

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Stay silent when you are called to account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought to book' looks like being held to account, but 'book' is the verb reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something safe is to protect or conserve it.

clue.text: The non-soldiers, in turn, enlist

indicators.note: in turn means the pieces are read back to front

parts.note: taken as written
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Civilians take their turn to join up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' turns NONGIS round.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up for military service is to join the forces.

clue.text: Able to read the title out "Time Held Captive"

indicators.note: held captive means one piece is locked up inside the other
out signals the letters of title are put out of order

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A title page announces a book called Time Held Captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TITLE to LITTE, and 'Held Captive' puts ERA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who can read and write has literacy.

clue.text: Achieving equality in pay, having a right to it

indicators.note: having means the pay word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Workers win equal pay, being entitled to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' puts R and IT inside PAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity means equal status or value, as in pay parity.

clue.text: Seems frightened by the many birds about

indicators.note: about says the birds surround the letter for many

parts.note: finches are small songbirds
L, Roman fifty, stands for many

explanation.surface: Someone appears scared by a flock of birds flying around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside FINCHES.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil or wince is to show fear.
